      "label": "HazardConsequence",
      "name": "Pool fire",
      "node_id": "H1",
      "node_type": "HazardConsequence",
      "evidence": "The report states, \"This case study examines a fire at the Environmental Quality Company (EQ) hazardous waste facility in Apex, North Carolina.\" It further says, \"Within minutes, the fire spread to the flammable liquid storage area, causing 55-gallon drums of flammable hazardous waste to explode and sending fireballs hundreds of feet into the air.\"",
      "explanation": "The incident is analyzed primarily as a large uncontrolled fire involving stored flammable liquid hazardous wastes. The report's main discussion centers on fire detection, fire control equipment, and lack of fire barriers that allowed the fire to spread. Drum explosions/fireballs and the toxic smoke cloud are treated as escalation effects and consequences of the main fire. Among the available labels, \"Pool fire\" is the closest match to the sustained flammable-liquid fire that drove the incident.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    }
  ],
